item.title: LAUTECH ASUU begins indefinite strike
item.description: By Adeola Badru Academic activities have been disrupted at Ladoke Akintola University of Technology (LAUTECH), Ogbomoso, Oyo State, following the commencement of an indefinite strike by the institution’s chapter of the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) on Thursday. The industrial action followed the expiration of a 14-day ultimatum issued by the union to the university management over outstanding demands, including the implementation of the 2025 Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN)-ASUU Agreement and the payment of consequential arrears dating back to January 2026. The union is also demanding the immediate payment of outstanding Earned Academic Allowances (EAA) and promotion arrears covering the period from 2013 to 2025. According to ASUU, the university’s Governing Council formally accepted and approved the implementation of the December 2025 FGN-ASUU Agreement. However, the union said the management had repeatedly cited a lack of funds as the reason for delays in implementation. Beyond the financial demands, the union is seeking the resolution of several administrative and governance issues before the Vice-Chancellor and the university management. These include concerns about the composition of the Staff Disciplinary Committee, the reconstitution of the Committee of Provosts and Deans, and transparency in the university’s electronic voting system. In a statement jointly signed by the branch Chairperson, Prof. Olujimi Dada, and the Secretary, Dr Soji Arinola, the union expressed frustration over the failure to resolve the issues despite repeated attempts at formal and informal dialogue. The union said it decided to embark on the indefinite strike after exhausting several avenues of engagement without reaching a resolution. It urged members to remain united throughout the industrial action and advised them to disregard information or directives not issued directly by the branch chairperson. The union stressed that only information and directives issued by the branch chairperson should be treated as authentic during the strike. item.title: 2027: INEC moves to address electoral risks in Ebonyi
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Ebonyi State has intensified efforts to identify and address potential risks that could disrupt the conduct of the 2027 general elections. The move followed a workshop on Electoral Risk Management organised at the commission’s headquarters in Abakaliki for stakeholders, including media representatives, security agencies and local government electoral officers. Participants identified potential threats to the elections, including snatching and destruction of electoral materials, abduction of election officials and the inaccessibility of some villages and communities. Speaking at the workshop, INEC Administrative Secretary in Ebonyi State, Mrs Joan Onyibor, said the exercise was timely given the proximity of the January and February 2027 elections. She explained that electoral risk management provided a structured and proactive approach to identifying, assessing, monitoring and mitigating threats that could compromise the electoral process. According to her, such risks could include security threats, political tensions, misinformation, environmental challenges, logistical constraints and other operational difficulties. Onyibor warned that failure to identify and address the risks could disrupt electoral activities, endanger voters and election officials, and undermine public confidence in the electoral process. Declaring the workshop open, the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Ebonyi State, Mrs Pauline Ugochi Onyeka, commended the Head of Planning and Monitoring, Mrs Mercy Amechi-Okorie, for organising the programme for stakeholders. Onyeka said strengthening the electoral risk management framework had become increasingly important as the 2027 elections approached. “We must move beyond responding to challenges only after they emerge and adopt a proactive approach that allows us to anticipate risks and address them before they develop into serious threats,” she said. She added that the workshop was designed to improve stakeholders’ understanding of electoral risk management, build institutional capacity and strengthen their ability to identify, document and report potential threats across different locations. The REC stressed that effective electoral risk management depended on close cooperation and timely information-sharing among INEC offices, security agencies, civil society organisations, the media and other stakeholders. “No institution can manage every electoral risk effectively on its own,” Onyeka said, calling for a coordinated approach to strengthen preparedness and response mechanisms. She said collaboration among stakeholders would help improve the security and integrity of the electoral process ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Reps seek review of NCC phone rules over price hike fears
item.description: By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has called for a review of the Nigerian Communications Commission’s (NCC) mobile device verification requirements over concerns that the policy could increase phone prices and lead to the wrongful blocking of legitimate used devices. The House warned that additional compliance costs under the framework could increase expenses for phone importers and retailers, with consumers, particularly low-income Nigerians, likely to bear the burden through higher prices. The resolution followed a motion sponsored by a Kano lawmaker, Sani Wakili, urging the commission to review the implementation of its device verification framework in consultation with relevant stakeholders. The framework, operated through the Device Management System and the Central Equipment Identity Register, enables the identification and verification of mobile phones and other SIM-enabled devices using their International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) numbers. Lawmakers noted that the enhanced verification requirements, which took effect on October 7, 2026, impose additional compliance obligations on newly imported devices, potentially raising operating costs for importers and retailers. They expressed concern that businesses could transfer the additional expenses to consumers, making mobile phones less affordable for Nigerians who rely on them for communication, education, banking and other commercial activities. The House also raised concerns about possible technical errors, database mismatches and limitations in the commission’s scanning and verification systems, warning that such challenges could result in legitimate devices being wrongly rejected or blocked. According to the lawmakers, the second-hand phone market could be particularly affected, given that used devices offer a more affordable alternative to new phones for many Nigerians. While acknowledging the NCC’s efforts to tackle counterfeit, cloned and stolen mobile phones, the House stressed that enforcement should not unfairly penalise legitimate businesses or restrict access to affordable communication devices. Consequently, the lawmakers urged the commission to review the framework’s implementation, simplify verification procedures and reduce compliance costs. They also called for a fair and accessible verification process for used and second-hand mobile phones to prevent legitimate devices from being wrongly flagged or blocked. To further examine the concerns, the House mandated its Committees on Communications and Commerce to engage the NCC and other relevant stakeholders on the implementation of the requirements and report back within four weeks for further legislative action. The Committee on Legislative Compliance was also directed to ensure compliance with the resolution. item.title: ‘I won’t waste my time talking about Amaechi’ — Oshiomhole
item.description: Senator Adams Oshiomhole has dismissed former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi as unreliable, saying he would not waste his time discussing the former minister. Oshiomhole spoke on TVC while reacting to Amaechi’s comments that President Bola Tinubu faces more challengers in the 2027 presidential election top challengers are from the South, while former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has fewer opponents because he is from the North. “If you know Amaechi, you won’t waste airtime talking about him,” Oshiomhole said. The former Edo State governor questioned Amaechi’s political consistency, citing his past dispute with Atiku over the African Democratic Congress presidential primary. According to Oshiomhole, Amaechi had accused Atiku of emerging from a fraudulent primary and challenged his victory in court. “Here is Amaechi on record in your TVC coverage and other network stations, who said that his own boss, the presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar, that the primary that produce him was a fraudulent process, and Atiku stole the mandate, he didn’t win the mandate. He didn’t stop there. Amaechi went to court to challenge Atiku that he stole the mandate,” he said. Oshiomhole added that Atiku later reached an agreement with Amaechi, claiming the former vice-president had asked him to share the mandate they allegedly obtained through a fraudulent process. “This is not social media, there are court documents, and Atiku went back to him and said okay, let’s share the stolen mandate together,” he said. Oshiomhole also referred to Amaechi’s political history, arguing that his rise to power and appointment as a minister were not the result of direct electoral victories. He said Amaechi became governor following a Supreme Court decision and was appointed minister by former President Muhammadu Buhari in 2015. “And I am not surprised that knowing what I know about him…he’s been very lucky that Supreme Court make him a governor without appearing on the ballot, and President Buhari made him a minister without voting for him in 2015, because I was a national player and later national chairman, so I know what I’m talking about,” Oshiomhole said. The senator further criticised Amaechi for describing other political figures as ethnic champions, arguing that the former governor had presented himself as the exception before the African Democratic Congress primaries. “He referred to Atiku as an ethnic champion. He referred to every other person as an ethnic champion. He was the only non-ethnic champion in the ADC before their primaries,” Oshiomhole said. He questioned Amaechi’s assessment of other political leaders, saying someone who dismisses others as ethnic champions should not be taken seriously when discussing leadership in a diverse country like Nigeria. item.title: Imo West: South-East Youths congratulate Okorocha, urge Uzodimma to respect the ruling
item.description: By Chinedu Adonu The South-East Youths Stakeholders Forum has congratulated former Imo State Governor, Senator Rochas Okorocha, following a Federal High Court judgment declaring him the winner of the All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial primary for Imo West ahead of the 2027 general elections. The forum also urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to comply with the court’s directives and take the necessary steps to recognise Okorocha as the party’s candidate for the district. The judgment, delivered on Thursday by Justice Obiora Egwuatu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, ordered Governor Hope Uzodimma of Imo State to stop presenting himself as the APC candidate for the Imo West senatorial election scheduled for January 16, 2027. The court held that evidence before it established that Okorocha secured the majority of votes cast during the APC senatorial primary conducted on May 18, 2026, which was monitored by INEC. It consequently directed the APC to submit Okorocha’s name to the electoral commission as its candidate for the election. The ruling followed a legal challenge by Okorocha against Uzodimma’s recognition as the party’s candidate. INEC’s previously reported official results had listed Uzodimma as the winner of the primary, a position Okorocha contested in court. Reacting to the judgment, the forum described the development as significant and expressed confidence that the rule of law would prevail in resolving political disputes. In a statement made available to journalists, the chairman of the forum’s Imo State chapter, Comrade Ifeanyi Nwosu, said respect for judicial decisions remained fundamental to democracy, justice, peace and political stability. The forum called on INEC to take the necessary steps to implement the judgment in accordance with the court’s directives and applicable laws. It also appealed to Uzodimma and his supporters to respect the ruling, embrace reconciliation and work towards a united APC ahead of the 2027 general elections. According to the group, unity, mutual understanding and collective commitment among party leaders and stakeholders are essential to strengthening the APC and advancing its electoral objectives. The forum further reaffirmed its commitment to mobilising youths across the South-East in support of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and APC candidates in future elections. It urged party leaders and stakeholders in Imo State to set aside their differences and work together in the interest of the party. item.title: 2027: INEC fears poll disruption in insecure areas
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has raised concerns that insecurity could disrupt or prevent the conduct of the 2027 general elections in some parts of the country. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, expressed the concern on Tuesday in Gombe while addressing participants at the North-East Zonal Interactive Staff Meeting and Operational Readiness Assessment for the 2027 general elections. Amupitan described insecurity in some parts of the country as a major challenge to the conduct of credible elections, calling for urgent and coordinated action by security agencies to protect the electoral process. He said he would engage the National Security Adviser, the Chief of Army Staff and other senior security officials upon his return to Abuja to discuss measures to address the threats and create a safer environment for the elections. The INEC chairman said the commission would adopt a proactive approach to electoral security rather than wait for threats to escalate before responding. He added that INEC was strengthening collaboration with the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, the Department of State Services, the Armed Forces and other relevant agencies through the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES). According to him, the collaboration is designed to improve intelligence-sharing, security coordination and operational preparedness ahead of the 2027 polls. The concerns come as INEC intensifies preparations for the elections, with insecurity posing potential risks to the movement of electoral personnel, distribution of sensitive election materials and participation of voters in affected communities. Amupitan stressed that sustained cooperation between electoral authorities and security agencies would be critical to ensuring that Nigerians could exercise their democratic rights without fear or intimidation. He said early intervention, effective deployment of security personnel and a coordinated response to security threats were necessary to prevent insecurity from undermining the credibility, inclusiveness and peaceful conduct of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Neville warns managers can need sacking ‘for their own good’ as Carrick fights on
item.description: Gary Neville says managers sometimes need to dismissed “for their own good” as Manchester United persist with under-pressure boss Michael Carrick. Carrick’s future at Old Trafford has been the subject of intense speculation after a miserable run of eight games without a win. Sunday’s 3-0 humbling at home to Bournemouth left the English giants one point above the Premier League relegation zone. United have won just two of 12 matches in all competitions this season, with a return of seven points from eight league games representing their worst start to a league season in 40 years. But former United and England midfielder Carrick, 45, remains in charge and is expected to give a pre-match press conference later Thursday ahead of the team’s league match away to Chelsea on Saturday. “I reckon what’s happened in the 24 hours after Bournemouth is that they (the United hierarchy) literally debated it (Carrick’s future) back and forth,” former Manchester United captain Neville said on the Stick to Football podcast. “I don’t know this, but they’ve debated it to the point where they’ve got themselves into a muddle, and thought, ‘we’ll just stay with him’. “I think staying with him is a result of the lack of planning, the lack of probably available options, the lack of decision-making around the two people that probably are available. That’s when you’re really struggling.” Neville, a former United team-mate of Carrick, added: “Sometimes a manager needs sacking for their own good. I needed sacking at Valencia. I was happy that they put me out of my misery.” – ‘Enough is enough’ – Both Eddie Howe, previously in charge of Newcastle, and former Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann have been touted as possible replacements for Carrick at Old Trafford. Carrick, however, appears to have the backing of the United faithful, being warmly applauded by fans as he made his way down the tunnel following the defeat by Bournemouth. Moments later a chorus of boos erupted as the players left the pitch as supporters made clear where they think the blame lies for United’s current malaise. Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after inspiring an impressive revival following the team’s struggles under Ruben Amorim — United secured third place in the Premier League and a return to the Champions League. The drastic decline this season is an all-too-familiar story for United supporters, who last witnessed a Premier League title triumph 13 years ago under Alex Ferguson. Neville believes the root of United’s woes is majority owners the Glazer family, saying “enough is enough” as he urged them to sell-up. The Glazers took control of the club in a controversial takeover in 2005. They remain majority owners after selling a minority stake to British billionaire businessman Jim Ratcliffe in 2024 . Neville, a longstanding critic, reiterated his call for the US-based family to sell. “There’s £1.2 billion ($1.6 billion) of debt in that football club, they’re hamstrung in some ways,” said Neville

item.title: Tinubu has broken Imo’s shackles — Okorocha hails court judgment
item.description: Former Imo State Governor Rochas Okorocha has praised President Bola Tinubu following a Federal High Court judgment recognising him as the All Progressives Congress candidate for Imo West Senatorial District, saying the ruling has broken the shackles holding the state. Okorocha spoke on Thursday while hosting his legal team after the judgment delivered by Justice Obiora Egwuatu of the Federal High Court in Abuja. The court ruled that Okorocha won the APC senatorial primary conducted on May 18, 2026, and ordered the party to submit his name to the Independent National Electoral Commission as its candidate for the January 16, 2027 senatorial election. The court also directed Governor Hope Uzodimma to stop parading himself as the party’s candidate. Reacting to the judgment, Okorocha thanked the judiciary for standing on the side of justice, describing the outcome as a victory for the people of Imo State. “I thank the judiciary for standing on the side of justice. I could imagine what would have happened in the state if they decided to twist justice. This is a victory for Imo State,” he said. The former governor also linked the judgment to the symbolic shackle on Tinubu’s traditional cap, suggesting that the President’s position had become clearer through the court’s decision. “This is also the first time the Imo people will understand the sign of the shackle on President Tinubu’s cap. By this judgment, the shackle on Imo State has been broken, and it is also evident that the President is tired of this nonsense and that he is not in support of it,” Okorocha said. He expressed gratitude to Tinubu, although he did not provide direct evidence that the President had intervened in the legal dispute or influenced the court’s decision. The judgment followed a legal battle in which Okorocha challenged INEC’s recognition of Uzodimma as the APC’s candidate for Imo West. The dispute attracted further attention earlier this month after INEC petitioned the police and the Department of State Services over a disputed document circulating online that purported to name Okorocha as the winner of the primary. INEC maintained that its official report recognised Uzodimma as the winner. Okorocha also addressed reports surrounding his alleged arrest, saying he deliberately refrained from commenting when the news broke. “When the news broke out that I was arrested, I refused to make any comments,” he said. He, however, questioned the documents presented during the dispute over the APC primary, particularly the claims that Uzodimma emerged through consensus and the discrepancies he alleged in the dates recorded in the documents. Okorocha questioned how a document could indicate that Uzodimma emerged through consensus when, according to him, individual scores were recorded. item.title: ‘Horrific’ Russian Drone Strike Kills 14 At Ukraine Train Station
item.description: A Russian drone slammed into a busy platform at a railway station in Ukraine’s Dnipro on Thursday killing at least 14 people in what President Volodymyr Zelensky called a “horrific” attack that demands a response from Kyiv’s allies. The strike came as Ukraine and Russia strive to uphold a fragile local ceasefire in the ravaged city of Oleshky — under Russian occupation since 2022 and where residents have faced months of food, water and medicine shortages. The truce was holding into its third day, both countries said, with the Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets announcing that he had “set out with the Ukrainian delegation towards Oleshky” through Belarus and Russia. But elsewhere, Moscow continued to pummel Ukraine. The strike at the Dnipro train station hit a platform “where a regular commuter train and a regular passenger train were standing”, Zelensky said. By early Thursday afternoon, Dnipropetrovsk regional governor Oleksandr Ganzha said the death toll from the strike had risen to 14. EDITORS NOTE: Graphic content / In this handout photograph taken and released by the Ukrainian Emergency Service on October 29, 2026, Ukrainian law enforcement officers work at the site of an air attack on the railway station in Dnipro, amid the Russian invasion of Ukraine. (Photo by Handout / UKRAINIAN EMERGENCY SERVICE / AFP) Another 14 had been wounded, he said, adding that six of them were in severe condition after suffering “multiple shrapnel wounds”, including an 11-year-old boy and a man who had “both legs amputated”. Zelensky slammed the attack as “horrific” and insisted that “sanctions against Moscow and its war machine must not be eased for as long as this Russian war continues”. Images released by Ukrainian emergency services showed bodies on the platform, rescuers helping victims to safety and two burnt-out passenger trains with their windows shattered. French President Emmanuel Macron reacted with outrage to the attack, stressing the need for “far more than a localised ceasefire” like the one in Oleshky. “It is intolerable that Russia continues to reject all proposals to this end, choosing instead to pursue escalation and target civilians,” he said on X. Zelensky slams sanctions relief Russia has fired drones on trains across Ukraine since the first days of its 2022 invasion — destroying hundreds of locomotives and killing several railway workers. Ukraine’s air force said it had intercepted three jet-powered drones in a daytime attack, but that a fourth evaded its defences and hit the station. In the aftermath of the attack, Zelensky refreshed his criticism of a deal struck this month between US President Donald Trump and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to ease some sanctions on Russia allowing Moscow to release diesel onto global markets. “How many such terrorist strikes has Russia carried out against our people since sanctions were lifted on some Russian oligarchs and the energy sector, instead of de-escalating,” he asked. item.title: Meet Nigerian Engineer Yinka Ogunbiyi behind machine that braids hair five times faster
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigerian-born engineer Yinka Ogunbiyi is gaining attention for developing HaloBraid, an automated hair braiding device designed to help professional stylists complete hairstyles up to five times faster while reducing the physical strain associated with hours of braiding. Ogunbiyi, a Harvard graduate and biomechanical engineer, recently demonstrated how the technology works, offering a glimpse into how automation could transform the hair and beauty industry, particularly protective hairstyles that often require several hours to complete. Unlike a machine that replaces the stylist entirely, HaloBraid is designed to work alongside professional hairdressers. The stylist first sections the hair, applies the necessary products and starts the braid by hand before feeding it into the device. The machine then handles the repetitive weaving along the length of the hair, allowing the stylist to finish and seal the ends. The innovation aims to reduce the time spent on braiding while easing the physical demands placed on stylists who spend long hours working with clients. It also seeks to improve the salon experience without removing the human skill involved in creating the final hairstyle. Ogunbiyi said the inspiration for the invention came from her personal experience of getting her hair braided from childhood and the challenges she repeatedly observed among both stylists and clients. “My braid story starts at age four, sitting between my mum’s legs as she braided my hair for the first time. Since then, I’ve spent thousands of hours getting my hair braided — and heard the same story from stylists and clients again and again: braiding is beautiful, but it takes too much time and too much strain,” she said. Drawing on her background in biomechanical engineering, Ogunbiyi said she recognised the need for a better approach and developed HaloBraid in collaboration with hairstylists, designers and other professionals. She added that the device was built with people close to her in mind, including her mother, hairstylists and aunties, as well as others around the world who understand the experience of spending hours in a salon chair. The venture has also attracted significant investor interest, securing $7 million in seed funding in a round led by Seven Seven Six, the venture capital firm founded by Reddit co founder Alexis Ohanian, who is married to tennis champion Serena Williams. The development adds to Ogunbiyi’s growing recognition in innovation and entrepreneurship. Her HaloBraid project previously won a $75,000 Harvard Innovation Prize, highlighting the potential of the technology to address a familiar challenge in the beauty industry. With its latest demonstration, HaloBraid is positioning itself as a technology that combines traditional hairstyling expertise with automation, potentially giving stylists more time to serve clients while reducing the repetitive work involved in braiding. item.title: Indonesians Celebrate Rain After Months Of Smoke And Suffering
item.description: Residents and firefighters in an Indonesian city long shrouded in a toxic haze brought on by months of wildfires rushed outside dancing and chanting as rain this week brought a welcome respite. On Wednesday night, exhausted volunteer firefighters jumped around in the puddles and kissed the ground in gratitude as another burst came down. “We were overjoyed; every one of us volunteers was so happy that we prostrated ourselves in gratitude. Praise be to God that there was finally rain,” firefighter Lukman El Hakim told AFP. TOPSHOT – Indonesian soldiers, tasked with fighting forest and land fires, celebrate as it rains in Banjar Baru, South Kalimantan province on October 28, 2026, following months of forest and land fires. (Photo by MUDA SAGALA / AFP) | MUDA SAGALA / AFP Intermittent rains have been falling in Palangkaraya, the capital of Central Kalimantan province on Indonesian Borneo, where devastating wildfires have raged since August. The city’s air quality index hit 4,000 this month, its worst ever measurement and more than 13 times the environment ministry’s threshold for pollution deemed “hazardous” to health. More than 11,000 people have been treated for respiratory infections in Palangkaraya during the months-long crisis that has also affected Indonesia’s neighbours with haze pollution. The World Health Organisation has linked exposure to air pollution, including high levels of tiny, airborne PM2.5 particles, to increased risk of illness and premature death. A volunteer (R) assists a woman with a nasal oxygen cannula at a shelter run by the Central Kalimantan Forest and Land Fire Smoke Response Coalition (RAKAT) to aid residents experiencing respiratory difficulties in Palangkaraya, Central Kalimantan.More than 11,000 people have been treated for respiratory infections in Palangkaraya during a months-long wildfire crisis. item.title: 2027: Abia CP warns politicians against violence, intimidation
item.description: …Orders parties to notify police before rallies . We ‘re for nobody, we ‘re for everybody – REC, urges candidates to accept results or seek redress in court By Steve Oko UMUAHIA – The Abia State Commissioner of Police, CP Wilfred Afolabi, has warned political parties and their supporters against violence, intimidation, inflammatory statements and destruction of property ahead of the 2027 general elections. This is as the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has declared its neutrality in the 2027 Abia governorship election, assuring all candidates that it will provide a level playing field for every contestant. CP Afolabi, who spoke at the signing of a peace accord involving the NEC, security agencies and political parties in Umuahia, urged parties to notify the police in writing before holding rallies, processions and other political activities to enable adequate security arrangements. The meeting, held at the Police Officers’ Mess, Umuahia, was attended by INEC’s Resident Electoral Commissioner in Abia, Prof. Sylvia Agu, heads of sister security agencies and representatives of registered political parties and campaign teams. The Police boss reaffirmed the command’s commitment to providing professional, impartial and adequate security for all candidates, parties and their supporters, irrespective of political affiliation. He disclosed that the command had strengthened its security architecture through intelligence gathering and analysis, crime mapping, the revamp of its Cybercrime Unit and improved operational response mechanisms. Afolabi also acknowledged Governor Alex Otti’s directive on adequate security for political campaigns and related activities. He pledged continued collaboration with INEC, other security agencies and political stakeholders to protect lives and property and ensure a peaceful electoral process. The peace accord, which followed a review of relevant electoral laws by the command’s legal officer, was subsequently read to the stakeholders before representatives of political parties signed individually, pledging to pursue their political ambitions peacefully. Speaking at the event, the REC, Prof. Agu, said the commission was committed to serving all candidates equally, irrespective of their political parties, while urging them to maintain peace before, during and after the election. “We are not working for any particular party; we are working for all of you here. We are going to deliver on our mandate, but we are asking you to conduct yourselves properly,” she said. The REC urged candidates to accept the outcome of a free, fair and credible election, advising those dissatisfied with the results to seek redress through the judiciary rather than resort to violence or discredit the electoral process. item.title: Five Things To Know Today
item.description: TUC rejects ₦70,000 transport allowance as proposed scheme could cost ₦465.7 billion The Trade Union Congress has rejected the Federal Government’s temporary ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance for federal workers, demanding a permanent salary increase instead. President Bola Tinubu during the inauguration of the APC PCC. The government agreed with the Nigeria Labour Congress on Tuesday to provide the allowance for six months, beginning in November. However, a Punch analysis estimates that the programme could cost ₦465.7 billion over six months if all 1.1 million employee records on the federal payroll qualify. This is an estimate, not an officially approved expenditure figure. TUC President Festus Osifo argues that earlier temporary wage awards were inconsistently implemented and failed to reach many eligible workers. Why it matters: What appeared to be a breakthrough in labour negotiations has exposed disagreement within organised labour. The government must now address both the affordability of its proposed intervention and workers’ demands for permanent improvements in income. Watch: The government’s response to the TUC, final eligibility rules, the funding source and whether the NLC–government agreement proceeds as scheduled. INEC meets today to decide fate of Pantami, Adebutu and other excluded candidates INEC The Independent National Electoral Commission is considering petitions from parties whose governorship candidates were excluded from its published list for the February 6, 2027 elections. INEC National Commissioner Mohammed Haruna confirmed that the commission would examine the matter at today’s meeting. Affected candidates include Isa Pantami of the PDP in Gombe, Ladi Adebutu of the PDP in Ogun and Aminu Gwarzo of the Nigeria Democratic Congress in Kano. Several exclusions followed disputes over party nominations and compliance with membership-register requirements under the Electoral Act. No final decision from today’s meeting had been verified at this editorial cut-off. Why it matters: The commission’s decisions could determine which candidates appear on governorship ballots and whether additional court challenges become necessary. Watch: INEC’s formal decisions, publication of corrected candidate lists and legal responses from affected parties. item.title: Alleged assault: Ivan Toney to stand trial in June 2028
item.description: England striker Ivan Toney will face trial over an alleged assault at a nightclub in June 2028, it was announced Thursday. The 30-year-old, who plays for Saudi club Al-Ahli, is accused of headbutting and punching Saber Da Silva at a club in the Soho area of central London last December. Toney appeared at London’s Southwark Crown Court on Thursday and formally entered a not guilty plea to a charge of assault occasioning actual bodily harm. During the five-minute hearing, a provisional trial date was set for the same court on June 12, 2028 by Judge Christopher Hehir, who told Toney he was “sorry” about the delay. “That’s a long way in advance and I’m sorry about that,” said Hehir. “As you may know, the crown courts are operating under a great deal of pressure. We have got a massive backlog of work for various reasons.” Toney was released on unconditional bail after the brief hearing. An earlier hearing was told the alleged assault happened at the 100 Wardour Street club during a confrontation between the defendant and Da Silva. It was heard the two men “squared up to each other”, before Toney allegedly “lunged forward and headbutted the complainant, followed by a few punches”. The former Brentford player has played for England 10 times, scoring one goal. He was a member of the 2026 World Cup squad but is not in the latest Nations League squad. item.title: Facebook partners Funke Akindele to promote Nigerian storytelling
item.description: By Juliet Umeh Social media platform Facebook has partnered with Nollywood filmmaker and actor Funke Akindele to promote Nigerian storytelling at the London and Lagos premieres of her new film, The Four . The partnership will support the film’s world premiere in London and its homecoming premiere in Lagos, bringing creators, celebrities and audiences together. Meta’s Head of Communications for Sub-Saharan Africa, Oluwasola Obagbemi, said the collaboration would highlight how Facebook helps creators connect with fans and build communities around shared interests. “Facebook has always been about connecting people, and our partnership with Funke Akindele brings that to life through film,” Obagbemi said. He said creators on Facebook could reach global audiences, build relationships with fans and earn money from original content. “Through our partnership around The Four premieres in London and Lagos, we’re celebrating the creators shaping culture, and helping more creators who share original and engaging content on Facebook to succeed,” he said. Akindele said she was pleased to partner with Facebook to take Nigerian stories to wider audiences. “African cinema has always had beautiful stories for the world to enjoy, and it’s exciting to have Facebook as a partner in bringing these stories to even more audiences globally,” she said. The partnership will also spotlight Nigerian creators in the country and in the diaspora. A creator-hosted space at the premieres will capture social content on how creators use Facebook to reach younger audiences and share Nigerian stories and culture beyond the country’s borders. Akindele announced the partnership on her Facebook page. The company said audiences could follow the Meta Africa, officialfunkeAkindele, Funke Akindele and Fanntv Facebook pages for behind-the-scenes content from the premieres. The collaboration, it said, celebrates Nollywood’s global reach and the creators and communities helping Nigerian stories travel. item.title: EPL: Man City braced for another tough test in Brighton repeat
item.description: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has warned his side to expect no let-up from Brighton this weekend when the teams meet again just days after a dramatic cup tie. League Cup-holders City edged the Seagulls on penalties to reach the quarter-finals on Wednesday after twice coming from behind to draw 2-2 at the Etihad Stadium. After making 16 changes between them, both Maresca and Brighton counterpart Fabian Hurzeler are set to revert to their full-strength sides when the teams meet in the Premier League at the Etihad on Saturday. Table-toppers City are level on points with champions Arsenal, while third-placed Brighton are just five points behind the leading duo. “They (Brighton) are in a brilliant moment,” said Maresca. “They are winning games, they are scoring goals. They are scoring many goals every game –- three, four, five, goals a game. “I’ve watched all their Premier League games since we started, and since the first day –- against Arsenal, (Crystal) Palace, Liverpool, they always go front foot, man to man. “We knew that this was a tough game and they’re going to be exactly the same on Saturday,” added Maresca. Brighton went in front after 30 minutes when Malick Yalcouye steered Georginio Rutter’s shot past Geronimo Rulli from five yards. Mateo Kovacic hauled City level 20 minutes later with a fine finish that curled into the far corner from 25 yards. Rutter restored Brighton’s lead two minutes after half-time, slotting home from Jaouen Hadjam’s cut-back. Vitor Reis deflected in Rayan Cherki’s 72nd-minute free-kick to equalise for City. Kovacic’s penalty was saved by Jason Steele in the shoot-out, but Rulli denied Brighton’s Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk to send City into the last eight. City’s season continues under the shadow of being found guilty last month on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules. The club have appealed and deny any wrongdoing, but face a severe sanction unless they overturn the verdict. No punishment has yet been announced, however, and Maresca — who has repeatedly stated his complete trust in City’s hierarchy — remains focused on on-field issues, with his side drawn at home to third-tier Bradford in the League Cup quarter-finals. “It’s a different competition but the ambition has to be the same,” said Maresca, who succeeded Pep Guardiola after the Spaniard stepped down at the end of last season following a trophy-laden decade at the Etihad. “This is a new project with new players, a new manager. It started three months ago. “We need to do our business. That is winning games and, at the moment, we are doing that.” The post EPL: Man City braced for another tough test in Brighton repeat appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Court sacks Uzodinma as APC senatorial candidate for Imo West
item.description: …orders INEC to recognise ex-Gov Okorocha By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja The Federal High Court in Abuja on Thursday nullified the emergence of Governor Hope Uzodinma as candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) for the Imo West Senatorial election slated for January 16, 2027. The court, in a judgment delivered by Justice Obiora Egwuatu, held that evidence before it established that Governor Uzodinma was not the valid winner of the primary election the APC conducted in the senatorial zone on May 18, which was monitored by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). According to the court, it was a former governor of the state, Senator Rochas Okorocha, who garnered the highest number of votes cast at the primary election and therefore ought to have been nominated by the party. Consequently, Justice Egwuatu ordered INEC to forthwith recognise Senator Okorocha and publish his name as the authentic candidate of the APC for the senatorial poll. It further issued an order barring Governor Uzodinma from presenting himself as the candidate of the APC for the election. item.title: Iran Guards says three tankers on fire after hitting mines in Hormuz
item.description: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said on Thursday that three oil tankers had caught fire after hitting mines while attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz. “Over the past 24 hours, three violating oil tankers exploded and caught fire after striking mines while attempting to pass through the unauthorised southern route of the Strait of Hormuz,” the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said in a statement. The vessels had “switched off all their radar and navigation systems” and disregarded warnings from the IRGC navy, the statement said. It was not immediately clear when the incidents occurred or which flags the tankers were flying. Since the outbreak of the war on February 28, Iran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil and gas consumption. The United States has in response imposed a blockade on Iranian ports. Iran’s armed forces have repeatedly accused US Central Command (CENTCOM), which oversees US military operations in the region, of encouraging vessels to use a southern corridor near the Omani coast that Tehran considers unauthorised. “The IRGC Navy states that the unauthorised route through the Strait of Hormuz is mined, and that vessel owners and crews are responsible for transiting these routes and should not pay attention to CENTCOM’s delusions on social media,” the statement said. Earlier on Thursday, the British maritime agency UKMTO said it had received a report of a ship on fire in the strait but gave no details about the cause or any casualties. It was not immediately clear if it was one of the three ships referred to by the Guards. The organisation also said it had captured a US reconnaissance drone during an operation in the Strait of Hormuz in a separate statement. “The IRGC Navy announced that its electronic warfare unit had successfully captured a US MQM-170 drone during an offensive operation in the western Strait of Hormuz,” the statement said. item.title: Stop the Bloodshed: Pyrates demands action from Tinubu, Kefas in Taraba
item.description: The National Association of Seadogs (Pyrates Confraternity) demanded decisive action from President Bola Tinubu and the Taraba State governor, Agbu Kefas, over the killing of at least 58 people in Binari community in Karim Lamido Local Government Area. The group also tasked security agencies to discontinue all peace arrangements that have enabled terror groups to rearm. The NAS Cap’n, Dr Charles Meribole, in a statement entitled ‘’ The Taraba Massacre: Another Bloodbath in Our Nation, ” condemned what he called ‘’senseless killings’’ of Nigerians, noting that it was ‘’barbaric, reprehensible and must not go unpunished “ Meribole, while mourning the dead, expressed disappointment with the response of Nigeria’s political leadership and the security agencies to recurring killings, especially in Northern Nigeria. He lamented that the over 20,000 Nigerians who have been killed since May 29, 2023, when President Tinubu assumed office, should jolt the President to rise to the full weight of his office as President and Commander-in- Chief of the Armed Forces and end Nigeria’s security crisis. ‘’President Bola Tinubu should recognise that the security of Nigerians is not a peripheral issue to be addressed when convenient or tackled with political rhetoric. It is a central test of his administration’s responsibility to Nigerians and obligation to his oath of office. ‘’ We implore President Bola Tinubu to translate his directives to the security agencies into measurable results. His orders to dismantle criminal networks must come with clear timelines, effective monitoring and consequences for failure. Those implementing security operations must be held accountable for their performance, and any official found to have compromised these efforts must face the appropriate consequences.’’ Meribole upbraided Kefas for attending the All Progressives Congress 2027 Presidential campaign (APC) North-West campaign flag-off, noting that traumatised people of Binari deserve empathy and not empty promises. He called on the security agencies to discharge their duties with renewed determination, stressing that since terror groups have demonstrated that they are remorseless, they should be treated with equal measure through sustained and decisive security operations. The statement read in part ‘’ President Bola Tinubu’s recent marching orders to dismantle terrorists and bandits’ enclaves, rescue kidnapped citizens and restore public confidence in the government’s capacity to protect lives and property must be pursued with sustained commitment. ‘’ There must be no retreat, no complacency and no room for compromise with those who terrorise innocent Nigerians. item.title: NFF warned me against inviting Mikel, Enyeama, Emenike — Oliseh
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Former Super Eagles coach, Sunday Oliseh, has revealed that the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) warned him against inviting John Obi Mikel, Vincent Enyeama and Emmanuel Emenike to the national team when he took charge, describing the trio as players who were causing problems for the federation. Oliseh, speaking on The Play Zone Podcast, however, said he regretted not heeding the warning, recalling his efforts to engage the players individually and resolve issues surrounding their involvement with the national team. “I regret not having listened to the NFF. Because when I took over the job, the first thing NFF told me was to stop inviting three of them (Mikel, Enyeama and Emenike) because they were chaotic to the NFF,” he said. Oliseh recalled travelling from Belgium to France to meet Enyeama, who was playing for Lille at the time, saying he held discussions with the former Super Eagles captain and clarified matters with him. He said he also travelled to London at his own expense to meet Mikel and Victor Moses, who were both playing in England at the time, but was disappointed when Mikel failed to attend the scheduled meeting. “I did the same thing for Obi Mikel. With my own money, not the NFF money, I went to the UK, sent a message to the clubs, sent a message to him (Mikel), sent message not only to him but also to Victor Moses, gave them an appointment at a bar that was accessible in the heart of London, with my assistant coach, for two of them to come and have meeting. “Now, of the two of them, who did not come to the meeting? Obi Mikel did not come to the meeting. Victor Moses came. Obi Mikel did not even respond to the WhatsApp message,” he said. The former midfielder suggested that Mikel might have considered himself bigger than the national team coach because he was playing for a major club. “Maybe because he’ll say, ‘I play for this big club now,’ but you see, that’s why they say sometimes Sunday (Oliseh) is direct. Where did you play that I did not play? What did you play that I did not play? “Even though the coach was not a footballer or not as big as you, the fact that they’ve given him that title ‘national team coach’, means you have to respect the position he’s holding,” Oliseh added. He described Mikel’s failure to attend the meeting as one of the biggest insults he had experienced but said he did not take the incident personally. According to Oliseh, Moses used the meeting to explain the issues troubling him about the national team, including some experiences Oliseh said he could relate to. Oliseh also spoke positively about Emenike, saying his experience working with the former striker contradicted what he had initially been told about him. He described Emenike as a gentleman and a respectful player, adding that he was among the greatest footballers he worked with and also credited Emenike’s influence as an important factor in Nigeria’s triumph at the 2013 Africa Cup of Nations.
